metadata.title: Shape transitions and rare reversals in the elephant random walk
metadata.author: Arjun Pemmasani
metadata.abstract: We study the shape of the elephant random walk with a fair first step. For every $N\ge3$ and reversal probability $0<\varepsilon<1/2$, the second difference of its law changes sign at most four times. This gives a unimodal-or-bimodal dichotomy for the superdiffusive limit at each fixed memory $a=1-2\varepsilon\in(1/2,1)$. A characteristic-function bound excludes flat intervals. The unimodal and bimodal densities have exactly two and four inflection points, respectively. Bimodality holds without computation for $a\ge4/5$. A certified computation classifies this law outside an interval of length less than $3.3\cdot10^{-15}$ around $a=0.6688128600146$; uniqueness of a transition inside that interval remains open. This addresses the fair-start case of a conjecture of Gu\'erin, Laulin, Raschel and Simon. For rare reversals we prove an explicit total variation bound between the number of steps disagreeing with the first step and a truncated Luria--Delbr\"uck law, together with a Landau local limit theorem with an explicit rate. When $\log N\le x=N\varepsilon\le2\log N$, every mode lies at distance $x\log x+\lambda_{\mathrm L}x+O(\sqrt{x\log x})$ from an end, where $\lambda_{\mathrm L}\approx-0.2228$ is the Landau mode. For even $N$, the origin and each end are equally likely at a unique reversal probability, with $N\varepsilon=2\log N-\log\log N-\log16+o(1)$. At this crossing, every even $N\ge8$ has exactly two symmetric modal intervals and a unique interior minimum, by finite certified computations and analytic bounds.
